title: Travel Problems
goal: Report a missing item or travel disruption, ask about options, and explain a health-related change of plan.

runs.text: A
missing
item cannot be found;
stolen
means taken without permission. Say what you know: “I can't find my passport” does not establish theft. A
claim number
or
reference number
identifies a report.
Delayed
and
canceled
describe different travel problems.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: My suitcase didn't arrive on the flight.

turns.en: My suitcase didn't arrive on the flight.

runs.text: Which flight were you on?

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Flight 246 from Denver. It's a dark green suitcase with a yellow tag.

turns.en: Flight 246 from Denver. It's a dark green suitcase with a yellow tag.

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: Do you have the baggage receipt?

turns.en: Do you have the baggage receipt?

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Yes. Could you explain how to make a report?

turns.en: Yes. Could you explain how to make a report?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: I'll take the details and give you a reference number.

turns.en: I'll take the details and give you a reference number.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: How can I check for updates?

turns.en: How can I check for updates?

runs.text: For a passport: “My passport was in my bag, and the bag is missing.” If you witnessed theft, say “Someone took my bag.” Ask “Where can I report this?” and “Who can advise me about replacing my passport?” Replacement procedures depend on the issuing authority and your location; the dialogue supplies no guarantee of immediate travel.
If someone returns an item: “That's mine—thank you for bringing it back.” If ownership is uncertain: “Could you describe it? I want to make sure it's the right bag.”

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: My flight was canceled. What options are available?

turns.en: My flight was canceled. What options are available?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: I'll check the next departures for your booking.

turns.en: I'll check the next departures for your booking.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: I need to arrive today. Is another route possible?

turns.en: I need to arrive today. Is another route possible?

turns.speaker: Agent

runs.text: I'll look, but I can't confirm that yet.

turns.en: I'll look, but I can't confirm that yet.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: Please also explain the refund options if I don't take another flight.

turns.en: Please also explain the refund options if I don't take another flight.

runs.text: This teaches a request for options, not a universal refund or compensation rule. For a train: “The departure board says canceled. Is there a replacement service?” For a closed gate: “I understand boarding has closed. Who can help me with the next step?”
A
baggage fee
is a baggage charge. Ask “What is this additional fee for?”
Strike
refers to a work stoppage.
Staffing shortage
means too few staff are available. A notice naming either cause does not tell you everything about rebooking or payment.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: I'm sick and may need to change my return date.

turns.en: I'm sick and may need to change my return date.

turns.speaker: Insurance representative

runs.text: What happened, and where are you now?

turns.en: What happened, and where are you now?

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: I'm in Harbor City. I saw a doctor today, and I need to discuss whether I can travel.

turns.en: I'm in Harbor City. I saw a doctor today, and I need to discuss whether I can travel.

turns.speaker: Representative

runs.text: I'll explain the information we need to review your claim.

turns.en: I'll explain the information we need to review your claim.

turns.speaker: Traveler

runs.text: What documents do you require? Please send the conditions in writing.

turns.en: What documents do you require? Please send the conditions in writing.

blocks.caption: Illness changes the plan · Traveler & Insurance representative & Representative

runs.text: Avoid assuming a doctor's note automatically establishes coverage. You may hear
tummy bug

for a stomach illness. You can describe what you're experiencing with “I've been vomiting” or “I have an upset stomach,” without choosing a diagnosis. “I hurt my back” describes an event; “I'm not fit to fly” is a claim you may need a clinician to assess. Ask “Who can advise me whether I should travel?”
With a companion: “I'm upset about this. I need a minute, then we'll work out the options.” Frustration can be real; you need not perform cheerful acceptance.
Fictional case: Flight 246 from Denver; green suitcase, yellow tag, baggage receipt available. Later, the return flight is canceled. Separately, use an illness role with no coverage decision made.
Report the missing suitcase. Partner asks for its description and flight. Supply the details and ask how to get updates.
Partner says the next route is not confirmed. Explain that you need to arrive today and ask about an alternative or refund option without claiming entitlement.
Explain the illness-related concern to an insurer. Partner asks for documents. Ask what is required rather than saying coverage is guaranteed.
Solo: read the staff questions and answer, then retell one case without the card. Change one known fact on the next attempt.
Possibilities:

“It's dark green with a yellow tag.” “What happens if I don't take the alternative flight?” “Could you send the document requirements?” Check that you distinguish observed facts, uncertainties, and the specific help requested. Health-reporting support follows in Chapters 80–87.
